skill.name: grilling
skill.description: Stress-test plans and designs through a structured, one-question-at-a-time interview that explores decisions, dependencies, and codebase evidence when available.
skill.summary: Structured questioning for stress-testing plans and design decisions.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: No static security findings were reported for this prompt-only skill. The reviewed instructions in SKILL.md focus on structured plan questioning and codebase exploration when useful, with no prompt injection or exfiltration intent found.

content.value_statement: Unclear plans often hide risky assumptions and unresolved dependencies. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through one focused question at a time.
actual_capabilities: Interview users about plans or designs before implementation
Ask one focused question at a time
Provide a recommended answer for each question
Review the codebase when a question can be answered from files
limitations: Requires user feedback to continue the interview
Does not replace expert legal, medical, financial, or safety review
Only explores codebases available in the current workspace
May be slower than open brainstorming for early ideas

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Plan
use_cases.description: Check a proposed feature for hidden assumptions, missing decisions, and implementation dependencies before work begins.

use_cases.title: Challenge a Technical Design
use_cases.description: Walk through architecture choices one at a time and clarify tradeoffs before writing code.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Stakeholder Review
use_cases.description: Practice answering likely objections and strengthen the reasoning behind a proposal.

prompt_templates.title: Grill My Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Grill this plan one question at a time. Give your recommended answer after each question: [paste plan].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a written plan

prompt_templates.title: Find Missing Decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me about this design. Focus on missing decisions, dependencies, and risks. Ask one question at a time: [paste design].

prompt_templates.title: Use The Codebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Stress-test this implementation plan. If the repository can answer a question, inspect it before asking me: [paste plan].

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Grill this architecture proposal until every major tradeoff has a clear decision and rationale. Ask one question at a time: [paste proposal].

output_examples.input: Grill my plan to add role-based permissions to our app.
output_examples.output: First question: Which roles need distinct permissions on day one? Recommended answer: define the smallest role set required for launch.

output_examples.input: Stress-test this migration plan before I start coding.
output_examples.output: First question: What rollback point is acceptable if the migration fails? Recommended answer: define a verified backup and restore path first.

output_examples.input: Review this product launch plan and find weak assumptions.
output_examples.output: First question: Which launch metric proves the plan worked? Recommended answer: choose one primary metric before expanding success criteria.

best_practices: Share the current plan, target users, constraints, and success criteria.
Answer each question before asking for the next one.
Let the assistant inspect available code when repository evidence can answer a question.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for broad brainstorming without a concrete plan.
Skipping questions before resolving the decision they raise.
Treating recommended answers as final decisions without checking domain constraints.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an assistant stress-test a plan or design through focused questions and recommended answers.

faq.question: Does it ask many questions at once?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the assistant to ask one question and wait for feedback.

faq.question: Can it inspect my codebase?
faq.answer: Yes, when the codebase is available and can answer the current planning question.

faq.question: Is this only for software projects?
faq.answer: No. It can review product, process, and design plans, but it is especially useful with code context.

faq.question: Does it make decisions for me?
faq.answer: It provides recommended answers, but the user remains responsible for final decisions.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
